four legs like ancient pillars crossing the far background, each foot landing with a slow shudder that ripples across every puddle in the clearing, each sole wider than the whole foreground log
a shadow sweeps the leaf litter from left to right, blotting the dappled light completely, sending a dry warm wind across the moss that flattens every spore-head in its path
a tail the width of a fallen tree drags through the upper fern canopy overhead, pulling three fronds completely from their stems and letting them spiral down into the little world below
a vast head descends from the green ceiling directly above, blotting the sky, the enormous jaw parting just enough to close around a whole fern crown at the edge of frame
a footprint already pressed into the mud at the far edge, brimming with standing water, forming a still lake big enough to mirror the entire canopy, one toe-groove the length of the whole clearing
dust and shredded bark rain steadily from the canopy, a soft golden curtain shaken loose by something immense passing just beyond the treeline, settling across every leaf and web in reach
a flank of grey-green hide fills the entire far background like a slow-moving cliff-face, the texture of each scale the size of a shield, the body rolling with each unhurried step
ripples move outward across the big puddle-lake in perfect slow rings, the ferns on the bank trembling in unison, the whole floor world answering something too large and too close to see

a neck rises from behind the root tangle at frame-left and simply keeps rising, climbing through fern layer and canopy layer, disappearing into unbroken green long before it reaches whatever carries it
two rear legs only, crossing the far clearing floor, each foot depressing the earth so the whole ground tilts fractionally, the ankle alone twice the height of the tallest mushroom in frame
a shadow arrives before anything else, a darkness rolling across the litter like a slow tide, the temperature dropping a degree, every mote of floating spore suddenly stilled inside the cool shade
a tail tip drags the lower fern fronds aside with a long tearing whisper, the bent stems slowly straightening afterward, releasing a green smell sharp enough to change the air of the whole glade
the underside of a vast jaw fills the sky above the puddle, the throat skin pale and loose, the whole head sweeping sideways in one browse-arc, combing the canopy edge clean
a single fresh footprint at mid-frame, the rain that fell minutes ago already collected into a clear bowl, a perfect mirror-lake pressed into the clay by one passing toe, already hosting a ripple
a cascade of broken bark chips and old leaf matter falls from above with no warning, pattering across every surface in the clearing, the canopy still shaking in slow waves after the source has passed
four legs mid-crossing, the near pair close enough that the hide texture is readable from below — deep-grooved, dusty, river-bark grey — each step compressing the earth with a low felt thud
a shadow passes across the still puddle and does not leave, the giant paused somewhere just out of frame above, the reflected canopy replaced by perfect unbroken darkness across the water
a length of tail hangs motionless through the fern ceiling for three long seconds before swinging out of frame again, the disturbed fronds still rocking, seeds drifting down from the impact
the head drops into frame from above and holds there, one enormous eye rotating slowly forward, the iris the full circumference of the biggest mushroom cap, utterly calm and amber-coloured

a fresh toe-print fills the left foreground, the walls of pressed clay taller than the tallest toadstool, a trapped beetle paddling slowly across the brown water collected inside the single impression
a lateral wall of dark hide moves slowly across the far background, no head, no tail visible, just texture and scale, the hide creased at a hip-fold big enough to shelter inside

the whole floor trembles in a low rolling pulse, every water surface gaining concentric rings simultaneously, every vertical stem leaning slightly then recovering, the disturbance moving from left to right across frame

the far legs only, two great columns vanishing upward out of frame, their passage through the undergrowth having already swept a clean corridor of flattened ferns stretching to the horizon behind them
litter lifts off the ground in a small scatter — seeds, beetle wings, a dry leaf — as a pressure-wave precedes something large approaching through the undergrowth just outside the frame's right edge
a neck curves away into the canopy at frame-right, the base of it at mid-frame still wide enough to dwarf the root buttress beside it, the upper body dissolved entirely into green
